title: The Pulse: What can we learn from the Railway hack?
author: Ivan Klaric
description: Cloud platform Railway published a detailed postmortem about their recent hack in which the attacker likely used no-safeguards AI models. Railway hardened its systems as a result.
summary: Hi, this is Gergely with a bonus, free issue of the Pragmatic Engineer Newsletter. In every issue, I cover Big Tech and startups through the lens of senior engineers and engineering leaders.
takeaways: Attackers have access to abliterated AI models, while the models Railway has for defense – from the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic – refuse to engage in cybersecurity activity, including defensive work.
Railway faced a couple of these: To simply notify customers that their API keys were leaked, or immediately notify vendors like Anthropic and OpenAI, sending over API key hashes?

Over the past two weeks I’ve talked with several CTOs and founders at infra companies, and in those circles, it’s an open secret that companies are being targeted by what looks like Chinese attackers, using abliterated AI models (those with no safeguards).
